blocks.text: CI builds once for the server's architecture and pushes an immutable tag; the server pulls that exact image and runs a prod Compose overlay with no builds, no published internal ports, restart policies, limits and log rotation.

$ export TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
$ docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t ghcr.io/acme/rag-api:$TAG --push \
    --cache-from type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/acme/rag-api:buildcache \
    --cache-to type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/acme/rag-api:buildcache,mode=max .
$ docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml pull && docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml up -d --wait
Compose on one VM is valid production for many internal services, with limits: brief gaps on recreate (no rolling updates), no multi-node failover, manual scaling.

Q: "How do you ship this stack to a server?" A: "CI builds for the target architecture, pushes a git-SHA tag, and the server pulls that exact image with a prod overlay: no build section, only the proxy published, restart policies, resource limits, log rotation, secrets from a store, and tested off-host backups."

items: Build once in CI, for the server's arch.
